about.title: Hidden Hills Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Hidden Hills is a small, gated community in Los Angeles County with just under 2,000 residents, and most who need hospital care or specialist treatment travel outside the city to get it. That means a malpractice claim involving a Hidden Hills resident often involves a hospital, surgical center, or physician's office located elsewhere in the county, which can add layers to how a case is investigated. We help residents sort through what happened after a bad medical outcome by reviewing the details and explaining your options under California law. California's MICRA law requires a qualified medical expert to review the case, a 90-day pre-suit notice before filing, and a claim brought within specific time limits. Because these cases require records review and expert testimony, having someone evaluate the details early matters. We offer a free case review, and you pay nothing unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Hidden Hills Families Should Know About These Claims

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally requires a malpractice claim within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the date it happened. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can be filed, California law requires sending the healthcare provider a 90-day notice of intent to sue, which affects how a case timeline is planned from the beginning.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically has to confirm that the care fell below an acceptable standard. A poor outcome by itself isn't enough — the law separates unfortunate results from actual negligence.

items.question: I live in Hidden Hills but was treated at a hospital in another city. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Not for our review process — we can still help you understand your case regardless of where the treatment occurred. What matters more is where the care was given and which laws apply, both of which we can sort out with you. Your Hidden Hills residence doesn't limit your options here.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having someone review the specific timeline of your case. Waiting too long can mean losing the right to pursue a claim at all.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. That's why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to evaluate the case. We can help you understand whether your situation meets that bar.
